English: Stone Outcrop
A rugged cluster of exposed stones and makeshift shelters marks the first step in exploiting the hills. Laborers gather loose rocks and begin to clear the land for future quarrying.
Quarry Shelter
A cluster of sturdy huts and covered workspaces provides shelter for workers and tools, increasing both productivity and safety in the quarrying process.
Hillside Pit
A shallow pit dug into the hillside, with simple timber supports and rough-hewn ramps, allows for the extraction of larger stone blocks from beneath the surface.
Block Cutters Shed
A permanent stone shed fitted with robust workbenches and simple cranes, allowing skilled masons to precisely cut and finish large stone blocks for construction and trade.
Hillsmens Lodge
A fortified lodge for foremen and quarry guards, offering protection for the workforce and a rudimentary administrative center for managing quarry operations.
Stone Hoist

The construction of treadwheel cranes and reinforced hoists enables the rapid and safe movement of massive stone blocks, improving output and attracting merchants seeking high-quality building materials.
Hills Guild
A formal guildhall organizes master masons, quarrymen, and stone merchants, securing lucrative trade contracts and overseeing apprenticeship programs to grow local expertise.
Rock Cart Track
A network of stone-paved cart tracks and waystations connects the quarry to the nearest town, greatly increasing trade throughput and the ability to export stone throughout the region.
Hillmans Keep
A commanding stone keep rises above the quarry, serving both as a powerful defensive stronghold and as the administrative heart of the hills' stone trade and labor force.
Highland Quarryworks

A sprawling complex of advanced quarrying operations, fortified depots, and merchant offices, the Highland Quarryworks dominates the hills, exporting stone and fostering prosperity across distant lands.
